correctness.rationale: Brownian entrance-law integration yields the normalized excursion-lifetime density and exact count overlap \(K(s,t)\). A compensated Poisson linear combination has \(L^\infty\) norm \(O(T^{-1/4})\) with exactly constant quadratic intensity; the characteristic-exponent Taylor remainder vanishes uniformly for each test vector, proving Gaussian fdd convergence. The integrated kernel is bounded after the \(T^{-5/4}\) scale; the same argument gives its Gaussian fdds, while a uniform \(\mathbb E|H_T(t)-H_T(s)|^2\le\kappa\sqrt L|t-s|^2\) bound proves C-tightness. Elementary integration verifies the explicit covariance. Differentiability of the smooth max term at positive t0 yields the Hurst-1/4 local Gaussian tangent. The model has dense infinite-count times, correctly restricting unintegrated counts to fdd claims. The standalone standard-library checker passed 1017 finite checks, which supplement but do not replace the proof.

evidence: Pang–Taqqu (2019) assume a locally bounded power-law response and finite Poisson arrival rate with centered independent mark distributions. Their limit covariance is a weighted convolution of response differences, not the present population-overlap covariance.
Marynych–Verovkin (2017) start with renewal interarrival times and only finitely many immigrating response processes by each finite time; their main limit is an inverse-stable-subordinator integral.
Seppäläinen (2005) treats particle current in a lattice independent-random-walk growth model, with no Brownian excursion immigration or dense blowup.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Generic Gaussian limits and Hurst-1/4 phenomena are established elsewhere, but the checked theorems do not directly satisfy the singular infinite-arrival and dense-exceptional-time hypotheses. A more general compensated-Poisson central limit theorem could imply the finite-dimensional Gaussian step; what is specifically asserted here is the combined model-specific continuous integrated limit, exact covariance, and local/global tangent distinction. Residual risk remains rather than claiming uniqueness.

value.rationale: The singular Brownian excursion model has finite population at each deterministic time but infinitely many live particles at a dense exceptional set; this prevents naive raw-path Gaussian limits. The combined theorem provides a nontrivial continuous limit for the physically meaningful cumulative population-time, its exact fluctuation variance \(4\kappa t^{5/2}/15\), and a structural distinction between globally nonstationary one-quarter-self-similarity and locally fractional-Brownian behavior. These properties determine uncertainty for time-aggregated particle observables and are not supplied by a scalar Poisson marginal or a textbook CLT alone.
